title: Decision: the account of a nick that cannot be written on the wire
description:
extended-join and account-tag carry the account of a nick, which in mimid is
the user's MIMI URI (docs/design/agent-frontends.md §7.15, the same string
311 RPL_WHOISUSER and 330 RPL_WHOISACCOUNT already send). A URI reaches the
front end from a peer's MLS credential and from the client's own line, and
nothing between the credential and the wire bounds it or keeps the characters
IRC cannot write out of it: `parse_user_uri` (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs)
rejects only an empty domain, an empty local part and a `/` in the local part,
and `Names::identity` copies whatever it is given into `Identity.uri`, so a
URI holding a space, CR, LF or NUL, one starting with `:`, one that is not a
user URI at all, or one long enough to carry the JOIN line past 512 octets is
reachable.

~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircv3-extended-join.md, "Description", defines two forms
of the JOIN message and no third:

    :nick!user@host JOIN #channelname accountname :Real Name
    :nick!user@host JOIN #channelname * :Real Name

and says of the second that it "represents that the user has not logged in to
an account prior to channel ingress", with "an asterisk is not a valid account
name". ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircv3-account-tag.md says the tag "MUST be named
`account`, and contain the sender's current services username. (If the user is
not identified to any services account, the tag MUST NOT be sent.)" Neither
gives a value for an account that exists but cannot be written.

READING A (chosen): write `*` as the account and as the realname, and send no
`account` tag. The two specs define exactly one other legal value each, and
both say the same thing to a client: this nick's account is not known to you.
A client parsing either form gets the parameter count and the tag grammar it
was promised.

READING B: leave the account and realname parameters off that one JOIN line
and send the plain three-token form instead. A client that negotiated
extended-join reads params[1] as the account (goguma 5aa7baa5
lib/client.dart), so the line would be parsed as a JOIN of three channels or
rejected, which is worse than a nick whose account is unknown.

READING C: write the URI with the offending characters replaced, as
`host_part` and `nick_part` already do for a hostmask. Rejected: an account is
compared for equality by the client against the account in 330 and in
WHOIS, and a substituted string would name a user who does not exist, which
is the one thing a credential-derived identifier must not do.

Where it is: `account_of` and `account_param` in
crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs, with MAX_ACCOUNT as the length limit,
both carrying a pointer here. The wider invariant — that an `Identity` minted
from a URI can always be written on the wire, which 311, 330, 352 and the
hostmask need as much as these two capabilities do — is bead mimid-1wgh.140.11.
close_reason: Settled from ircv3-extended-join.md and ircv3-account-tag.md during bead mimid-1wgh.140.6: `*` as the account parameter and realname, and no `account` tag, for a user URI that is not a user URI, is longer than MAX_ACCOUNT or cannot be written as a middle parameter. names.rs's account_of and account_param carry the pointer, with the unit test an_account_that_cannot_be_written_has_none; the wider invariant is bead mimid-1wgh.140.11.
